correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western headward arm and its northeastern connection
correspondence.finding: The Pedro do Rosário original depicts the western arm near the São Francisco/Coelho and Penha setting joining the Bamburral corridor. Its northeastward approach and receiving junction correspond to the selected opening at ordinary geographic scale. The generalized stored opening does not follow the source line vertex for vertex; this is not treated as a missing regional connection. The Bamburral label is not extended to establish a separate name for the entire initial arm.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward receiving course, lateral joins and transition toward the lowlands
correspondence.finding: The original labels Rio Bamburral at the upper receiving branch and depicts the continuous northward course past Lagoa/Três Palmeiras and the São Vicente Ferrer boundary setting. It shows the eastern Santa Rosa and Rio Grande branches and the western feeder junction farther north. These side branches are distinguished from the selected through-route. The selected continuation reaches the northward bend into the lowlands without a missing through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern transition and lowland course south of Pinheiro
correspondence.finding: The overlapping Pedro do Rosário and Pinheiro sheets depict the continuation north and northeast past the Roque/Ilha III and Lago Novo setting. The Pinheiro original prints Rio Pericumã on this continuous course and farther north near São José dos Crentes. Its lateral drainage and the river through the surrounding lowland mosaic remain connected. No separate named lake crossing is required to connect these selected parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Pinheiro approach, town-side river and northeastern turn
correspondence.finding: The Pinheiro original continuously depicts the selected river past the Vitória dos Bragas/Juçareira setting, along the eastern side of Pinheiro and through the northeastern turn toward Comporta. Local feeder joins and the river's connection through the lowland setting are visible. Nearby settlement names such as Lago Novo and Lago de Areia are not automatically treated as names of water bodies crossed by the line.

correspondence.component_scope: Managed Comporta/barrage passage and downstream river
correspondence.finding: The Pinheiro original shows the river continuing through Comporta and into the wider northeastern channel beside Ilha das Pedras. The state public-security report identifies the Pericumã barrage at Pinheiro and describes a field visit by boat and water passing its gate. Together they establish the ordinary managed river passage. No present gate position, discharge, safety condition or current operating claim is inferred from the historical report.

correspondence.component_scope: Stage-3/stage-2 join and northeastward lower river
correspondence.finding: The Pinheiro and Bequimão originals overlap on the same continuous river at the selected fragment boundary. The Bequimão sheet follows its northeastern bends along the municipal boundary with Central do Maranhão and repeatedly labels Rio Pericumã. The stored route generalizes several meanders, but its river corridor, intervening bends and connections are identifiable throughout.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Pericumã estuarine corridor and actual selected end
correspondence.finding: The Bequimão original depicts the selected lower Pericumã corridor opposite the Tavares setting and shows the river continuing downstream into a wider marine inlet. The final rendered northward stub is displaced from the map's river centerline; ordinary terminal correspondence is to the same adjacent estuarine reach, not an independently named northern tributary or an exact bank location. The selected end remains upstream of the broad inlet and cannot be described as the complete Pericumã ocean mouth solely because its stored terminal class is sea.

correspondence.component_scope: Western chosen opening and first eastward corridor
correspondence.finding: No inspected source traces the chosen western feeder, its initial joins or its entry into the eastward selected drainage.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle corridor north of Los Menucos and southern elbow
correspondence.finding: Olivares2020 supports regional interior-alluvial-aquifer context around Los Menucos. The aquifer polygon and field example do not trace the selected surface channel or demonstrate its southward elbow and eastward continuation.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward interior course and approach to the northern turn
correspondence.finding: No inspected corridor-scale source continuously identifies the selected eastward reaches or their convergence before the northern turn. Nearby locality names and modeled continuity are not used as hydronyms or through-link evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern turn and Sierra Colorada setting
correspondence.finding: The two groundwater publications identify Sierra Colorada regionally, but neither supplies an inspected source depiction of the selected approach, local crossing and eastward exit.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern lower approach and actual inland endpoint
correspondence.finding: The retained2013 prose names Laguna Carriló and Salina Lauriente near the southern edge of its study, but does not place the selected last reaches or endpoint within either waterbody. The2020 thematic map supplies no named receiver or selected final through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Nevada opening and northwestward feeder
correspondence.finding: The chosen southern opening lies in a mapped intermittent drainage east of Big Mud Lake. The channel follows the northward ravine and western tributary bend near Barrel Springs, then reaches the eastern Cow Head basin margin. The generalized bends remain within this connected drainage corridor at ordinary map scale. Barrel Springs is a spring label; no creek name is assigned from it, and the selected route does not traverse Big Mud Lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Cow Head wetland approach and Cow Head Slough
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation follows the mapped channel along the eastern Cow Head wetland margin, then the explicitly labeled Cow Head Slough northward past the Twin Lakes setting into Twelvemile Creek. The selected route follows the slough rather than crossing the central Cow Head lakebed or either Twin Lake. The northern junction and each intervening selected join are depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Twelvemile Creek border reach and Twentymile Creek canyon
correspondence.finding: The eastward border reach corresponds to labeled Twelvemile Creek. Its canyon turns around Dunn Butte and continues north in the labeled Twentymile Creek corridor. The mapped junctions and selected continuation through the Oregon–Nevada border setting are visible; neither nearby Horse Creek nor the western Fifteenmile Creek is substituted for the chosen reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Twentymile outlet, managed South Warner Valley and approach to Crump Lake
correspondence.finding: The selected route exits the Twentymile canyon, bends around the south side of the broad South Warner wetland and continues north toward Crump Lake. Cartography depicts channels, ditches, wetlands and the Highway 140 crossing throughout this corridor. The 2019 partnership account describes Twentymile and Deep Creek flow spreading through wetlands toward Pelican and Crump lakes and subsequent channel straightening and irrigation diversions. The State Engineer account describes northward drainage toward Crump. Together these establish the ordinary seasonal and managed passage without asserting one continuously flowing channel or present diversion operations. The selected path does not enter Greaser Lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Crump Lake south-to-north passage
correspondence.finding: The selected northward series lies within mapped Crump Lake and its southern wetland approach, west of Fisher Lake. The full lake passage is visible and the northern continuation reaches the narrow outlet corridor toward Hart Lake. Crump Lake is a lake name, not a river name for the whole selection.

correspondence.component_scope: The Narrows, Crump–Hart connector and Hart Lake
correspondence.finding: The mapped channel labeled Deep Creek links the north end of Crump Lake through the constricted Narrows setting to southern Hart Lake. The selected westward bend and succeeding northern parts cross Hart Lake, with Honey Creek entering from the west. The partnership report identifies the Narrows as the Crump–Hart division and names both lakes. All selected joins and the intervening lake passage are accounted for.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Hart Lake and Anderson–Swamp wetland corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected line leaves northern Hart Lake through the mapped channel and marsh belt, passes west of Anderson Lake and continues through the Swamp Lake wetland setting. The historical State Engineer findings describe Hart overflow continuing north through sloughs and lake depressions in high-water conditions. That authorial drainage description and the continuously mapped lowland corridor establish the generalized through-passage; the route is not required to cross each named lake center.

correspondence.component_scope: Flagstaff, Upper Campbell and Campbell lake passages
correspondence.finding: The mapped wetland approach reaches Flagstaff Lake. The selected eastward and northeastward continuation traverses the southern Flagstaff–Upper Campbell lake and marsh setting, then the Campbell Lake margin toward Stone Corral Lake. The original cartography distinguishes the lakes and connecting lowland, and the independently read historical drainage account identifies this northern chain as the high-water route toward Bluejoint. These are distinct lake names within a seasonal drainage corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Stone Corral connection and actual Bluejoint Lake ending
correspondence.finding: The final northeastward sequence follows the Stone Corral Lake margin and mapped connecting channel–wetland corridor at the foot of Poker Jim Ridge into Bluejoint Lake. The actual supplied ending lies within the mapped Bluejoint Lake wetland/lakebed. Both the chain identity and high-water passage are supported. No onward route beyond the selected ending, present lake level or exact shoreline position is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastern opening and initial south-southwestward Inland Ice passage
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening and entire first part occupy the broad mapped Inland Ice east of the Sermersuaq / Steenstrup Gletscher label. The original distinguishes this interior ice from the western exposed-rock coast. The opening, initial bends and joining position are geographically covered. Neither the glacier label nor the ice contours establishes a natural-river source or river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle southward Inland Ice sequence and approach to the westward turn
correspondence.finding: Both long middle parts continue south-southwestward within the mapped Inland Ice, approaching the westward bend inland of the coastal rock belt. The source covers every selected portion and their intermediate joining position. Blue surface-contour and ice-thickness markings and dark sub-ice bedrock contours are contextual glaciological information, not surveyed river-channel or throughflow evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward and southwestward ice passage
correspondence.finding: The westward turn and all eight subsequent short parts lie in the mapped ice terrain east of the exposed-rock coastal belt. The full westward succession and its southern turn are visible in the original. The nearby closed dark contour is sub-ice bedrock relief; it is not treated as a lake or a selected lake passage. No river hydronym or surface or subglacial hydraulic connection is established.

correspondence.component_scope: South-southwestward lower ice passage and exposed-rock-margin approach
correspondence.finding: The following three parts descend south-southwestward across the mapped ice-margin setting toward a small exposed-rock projection northeast of Kullorsuaq. Their joining positions, the ice-side approach and the final rock-margin transition are all covered at ordinary regional scale. The colored rock units and adjoining ice boundaries account for the geography without establishing a named watercourse across that transition.

correspondence.component_scope: Final short westward parts and actual selected ending
correspondence.finding: All nine final short parts and their joins occupy the generalized exposed-rock and coastal ice-margin setting northeast of the Kullorsuaq label. The actual selected endpoint is accounted for in the small rock-projection/coastal-margin setting, rather than assigned to a nearby named glacier or fjord. The model sea classification does not independently establish an ordinary river mouth. Exact contemporary ice-front, bank and terminal land/ice/water placement are not claimed.
